summary: Steel guyed fire tower in Algonquin Park, torn down in the 1950s per firelookout.ca; a 2025 trail guide dates a Cache Lake tower to the 1970s.

facts.design: Steel, guyed tower with an octagonal cupola
facts.status_note: Torn down, according to firelookout.ca. No source describes what remains at the site.

access.note: Track and Tower Trail in Algonquin Provincial Park, open year-round. The guide ties part of the trail's name to the old Skymount site.

visit.trail_note: The trail runs roughly through the centre of Algonquin's Highway 60 corridor. No tower stands to climb.

events.note: Not shown on the Department of Lands and Forests Tower Detection System Map (1963), per firelookout.ca.

notes_for_editor: Probably a duplicate of ca-on-skymount-2: same name, source page, district and elevation. Date conflict: firelookout.ca says torn down in the 1950s; the 2025 guide says a fire tower at a Cache Lake lookout stood until the 1970s and does not say whether it is the same tower. Location conflict: firelookout.ca says both Algonquin Park and Archipelago Township, Parry Sound District, and marks the coordinates (45.564998, -80.565809) as approximate. As far as place names in the guide allow me to judge, that point lies well west of the Highway 60 corridor (between the Dwight and Whitney gates), so the coordinates need checking. No build year, staffing or fire history found. Record status 'unknown' set to gone from the torn-down note.
